claude.result:
Braces balance and the file structure looks solid. The two `.def.name` bugs (which would have thrown runtime errors on two of the events) are fixed, dead code removed, and a responsive overflow fix added. The file is self-contained, uses no external resources or storage, and implements all 13 required systems with a documented deterministic turn order.

**Summary of what's in `game.html`:**
- Deterministic mulberry32-style seeded RNG (no `Math.random` anywhere)
- 8×8 seeded terrain map with adjacency-bonus buildings (Mine, Condenser, Greenhouse, Forge, Generator, Workshop, Storm Shelter, Trade Post, Housing)
- Two-stage production chains (ore→metal, ash→soil→food) with storage caps and overflow logging
- Individual colonists with job/skill/fatigue/morale, assignment UI, skill growth, morale-driven consequences (quit/refuse work)
- 10-node research tree with prereqs and real production/mitigation effects
- 13 events (5 with genuine tradeoff choices), weighted deck with cooldowns
- Caravan trading every 5 turns with stockpile/drift-based pricing
- Ashstorms every 6 turns with scaling severity, mitigation buildings/research, and repairs
- Save/load via textarea (JSON, validated, no browser storage)
- Win/lose conditions with a scored summary overlay
- Tabbed UI (Map/People/Research/Trade/Log/Dev), tooltips, keyboard shortcuts (Space, 1-5), responsive down to 360px
- Dev panel: 18 test assertions + a 200-turn deterministic benchmark with hash verification

Note: I wasn't able to get Node execution approved in this sandbox to run an automated smoke test, so I instead did a full manual line-by-line static review and caught/fixed a real bug (two events referenced a non-existent `b.def.name` instead of `bDef(b).name`, which would have thrown on firing). I'd still recommend opening the file in a browser and clicking "Run Tests"/"Run Benchmark" in the Dev tab to confirm live.
